CLINICAL ARTICLES

Real cases, explained.

Real X-rays from six cases, from arthritis to fractures. Each one explains what the images show, the treatment and the healing time.

01

TOTAL KNEE REPLACEMENT

Severe knee arthritis treated with total knee replacement

X-rays show a knee worn down by arthritis, then rebuilt with a total knee replacement. Read the full recovery timeline.

Full recovery: 1–3 monthsRead the case ↗
02

PARTIAL KNEE REPLACEMENT

Arthritis on one side of the knee treated with partial knee replacement

Only the worn inner compartment was resurfaced, keeping the healthy parts of the knee. Recovery is often faster than with a total replacement.

Full recovery: 6–12 weeksRead the case ↗
03

ELBOW FRACTURE

Elbow fracture: radial head fixation with a compression screw

A broken radial head in the elbow was fixed with one buried screw, allowing early movement to prevent stiffness.

Bone healing: 6–8 weeksRead the case ↗
04

HIP FRACTURE

Left hip fracture: reading the X-ray and planning recovery

A fracture through the trochanteric region of the left hip, explained from the X-ray with the usual treatment and healing timeline.

Bone healing: 12–16 weeksRead the case ↗
05

HIP REPLACEMENT FOR FRACTURE

Displaced hip fracture treated with hip replacement

A badly displaced right hip fracture was treated with a long-stem hip replacement, allowing early full weight-bearing.

Full recovery: 2–3 monthsRead the case ↗
06

THIGH BONE FRACTURE

Fracture above the knee fixed with a locking plate

A multi-fragment fracture just above the knee was rebuilt with a locking plate. See the X-rays and the full healing plan.

Bone healing: 12–16 weeksRead the case ↗
